_comment: Phase-4 E16 campaign-wide chunk-role census. Each chunk is classified by its OWN subtype marker (u32 at decompressed offset 0), read from the bytes rather than inferred from load order, across every LEVEL*.RAW. Regenerate: tools/phase4_e16_chunk_census.py

marker_space.0x0101: mesh definition (+4 object id, +0x0A sub-mesh count)

UNKNOWN_MARKER_ANALYSIS_2026-08-04.finding: All 74 previously-unclassified chunks are IMAGE RESOURCES: each carries a self-describing header whose u16 fields hold plausible pixel dimensions (320x256, 256x256, 160x132, 64x64, ...). They are not an unknown data family; they are pictures.

three_independent_lines: every one of the 17 chunks has the IDENTICAL header (0x20,0,320,0,256,0) and the IDENTICAL size 163,856
bit15 is clear on all 20,000 sampled pixels, as expected for opaque RGB555 (the PS1 mask bit)
pinned_family.corroborates: committed canon 'Loading screens = GFX/*.RAW ... 320x256 RGB555 chunk'
pinned_family.role_corrected_2026-08-04: sky/backdrop resource (feeds the sky-colour cache 0x800771BC/C0/C4), NOT a loading screen -- see LOADER_DECODE_2026-08-04

NOT_pinned.why: size arithmetic ALONE cannot determine (header size, palette presence, bpp, frame count). A permissive search 'solved' 74/74, but a uniqueness check found ZERO of the 74 are uniquely determined: every chunk admits 2-12 distinct (hdr, palette, dims, bpp, frames) combinations that reproduce its byte size exactly. The tidy first-hit answer was an OVER-FIT and is recorded here as refuted rather than banked.
NOT_pinned.leading_candidates_only: the most common consistent shapes were (12B hdr + 768B palette + w*h at 8bpp) for the 0x30-0x53 run and (16B hdr + w*h*2) for 0x28-0x2A -- plausible, unproven
NOT_pinned.status_update: PARTLY RESOLVED by the loader read: the 12-byte header + preamble-at-+8 layout is now code-confirmed for the texture-page class, which was the dominant ambiguity. The remaining unknown is per-family field MEANING (which u16 is width vs height vs VRAM coordinate) for markers 0x26/0x28-0x2A/0x30-0x5C.

UNKNOWN_MARKER_ANALYSIS_2026-08-04.decisive_next_step: read the LOADER that consumes these chunks and see how it interprets the header. The committed census already records a loader_caller (0x8003A4EC for LEVEL01 chunk 15). That is static resident-EXE work; it does not need a movie.
UNKNOWN_MARKER_ANALYSIS_2026-08-04.methodological_note: Recorded so the next pass does not repeat it: for self-describing binary resources, matching a size formula is NOT evidence unless the fit is shown to be UNIQUE. Always count the alternative fits before claiming a layout.
UNKNOWN_MARKER_ANALYSIS_2026-08-04.superseded_2026-08-04: The 'all 74 are images' framing here is SUPERSEDED by MARKER_SPACE_FULLY_MAPPED_2026-08-04: 46 of the 74 are pointer-registered blobs the loader never interprets. Retained to keep the reasoning trail visible.

LOADER_DECODE_2026-08-04.function: high_heap_loader_level_raw_decompress_orchestrator 0x8003A318 (asm/hand_written/8003a318_high_heap_loader.s); the census's recorded loader_caller 0x8003A4EC is a site inside it
LOADER_DECODE_2026-08-04.marker_is_code_confirmed: immediately after `jal 0x8001A1DC` (level_raw_lzss_decompressor) the loader executes `lw s4,0(fp)` -- the subtype marker is a u32 at decompressed offset 0, read by the retail loader itself, not an inference from data shape.
LOADER_DECODE_2026-08-04.class_split_is_code_confirmed: `slti v0,s4,32` / `beq` splits markers < 0x20 (texture/VRAM pages) from the structured families >= 0x20. The full dispatch chain compares 32, 34, 35, 36, 257, 258, 259, 260 (0x20, 0x22, 0x23, 0x24, 0x101..0x104) -- exactly the marker space the census found in the data.

texture_page_path.fields: reads u16 at +4 and +6 (staged into a libgpu RECT at sp+32/34) and u16 at +8 and +0x0A
texture_page_path.data_pointer: LoadImage(rect, s3 + 12 + round_down_even(u16@+8)) -- so PIXEL DATA BEGINS AT chunk + 12 + even(u16@+8).
texture_page_path.significance: This CODE-CONFIRMS the 12-byte header + preamble layout that size arithmetic could only guess at. The '768-byte palette' hypothesis is real: 768 is simply the value of the +8 field for that family. The loader then advances rect.x by rect.w and re-uploads, i.e. a tiled VRAM upload loop with a 768/192 VRAM-region bound.
texture_page_path.special_case: marker 29 (0x1D) additionally clears a small byte range near 0x800A-1464..-1461.

marker_0x20_path.the_key_step: the u16 at +16 is decoded as RGB555 -- `andi 0x1f` for R, `>>5 & 0x1f` for G, `>>10` for B, each scaled 5-bit->8-bit by multiplier 0x84210843 -- and stored to gp-relative 29116 / 29120 / 29124.
marker_0x20_path.CORRECTION_multiplier: An earlier revision and its positive test said 0x84218421. Direct pristine reads pin 0x8003AE14 = lui a1,0x8421 and 0x8003AE24 = ori a1,a1,0x0843, so the actual constant is 0x84210843.
marker_0x20_path.independent_corroboration: those are EXACTLY the per-level sky-colour cache addresses the committed starry-night mod patches (memory abl-gpu-injection-starry: '0x800771bc=R / 0x800771c0=G / 0x800771c4=B').
marker_0x20_path.inference_flagged: given the exact size arithmetic (16 + 320*256*2 = 163,856), offset +16 is where the image data begins -- so the sky colour appears to be sampled from the image's FIRST PIXEL. The decode and the destination globals are code-confirmed; 'first pixel' is the one inferential step.

LOADER_DECODE_2026-08-04.CORRECTION_to_my_earlier_claim: Earlier today I pinned marker 0x20 as a '320x256 RGB555 full-screen image' corroborating the committed GFX loading-screen format. The pixel geometry stands (320x256 16bpp, exact size match, bit15 clear). The ROLE was wrong: the loader feeds this chunk's colour into the per-level SKY-COLOUR cache, so 0x20 is the SKY/BACKDROP resource, not a loading screen. Loading screens live in GFX/*.RAW, a different container.

dispositions.<0x20: texture/VRAM page -- LoadImage(rect from +4/+6, base + 12 + even(u16@+8)); tiled upload loop
dispositions.0x20: sky/backdrop -- decodes u16@+16 as RGB555 into the sky-colour cache 0x800771BC/C0/C4
dispositions.0x21..0x26: individual arms. 0x22 = sprite/animation strip container; 0x23 = a straight 1,792-byte memcpy from chunk+4 into the fixed RAM table 0x800949B8 (which is exactly why every 0x23 chunk is 1,796 bytes); 0x24 = backdrop panorama, header 16B, data at +16, uploaded via level_texture_upload 0x8003CC58
dispositions.0x28..0x2F: POINTER-REGISTERED: TABLE[marker] = chunk base, at 0x8009C170 + marker*4 (8 slots)
dispositions.0x30..0x57: POINTER-REGISTERED: TABLE[marker] = chunk base, at 0x8009B4E8 + marker*4 (40 slots)
dispositions.0x58..0x5F: POINTER-REGISTERED: TABLE[marker] = chunk base, at 0x800A6450 + marker*4 (8 slots)
dispositions.0x101..0x104: mesh definition / mesh payload / collision planes / collision sector-source

the_74_unknowns_resolved.note: every previously-unclassified chunk now has a known loader disposition

MARKER_SPACE_FULLY_MAPPED_2026-08-04.why_size_arithmetic_could_never_work: 46 of the 74 (the three pointer-table ranges) are REGISTERED BY POINTER and never interpreted by this loader at all -- it records where the chunk is and moves on. Their internal layout is decided by whatever consumer later reads TABLE[marker]. No amount of size arithmetic on the chunk bytes could have determined a format the loader never imposes.
MARKER_SPACE_FULLY_MAPPED_2026-08-04.CORRECTION_the_74_are_not_all_images: Earlier in this same pass I concluded 'all 74 unknown chunks are IMAGE RESOURCES' because their headers carry dimension-looking u16s. That is wrong for the 46 pointer-registered ones: the loader treats them as opaque blobs. The claim survives only for the 0x20 family (image data whose first pixel seeds the sky colour). Dimension-shaped numbers in a header are not evidence of an image when the code never reads them as one.
MARKER_SPACE_FULLY_MAPPED_2026-08-04.next_step: find the CONSUMERS that read the three tables (0x8009B4E8 / 0x8009C170 / 0x800A6450); those consumers, not the loader, define the formats of the 46 pointer-registered chunks.
MARKER_SPACE_FULLY_MAPPED_2026-08-04.SUPERSEDED_the_46_are_not_images_2026-08: See REGISTERED_CHUNKS_RESOLVED_2026-08-04: the 46 pointer-registered chunks ARE images (frontend VRAM resources), consumed by three deferred-upload sites. The 'not images' framing here over-corrected an earlier over-claim.

REGISTERED_CHUNKS_RESOLVED_2026-08-04.question: The loader registers 46 chunks (markers 0x28..0x5F) by POINTER into three range-indexed tables and never interprets them, so their format belongs to whoever reads TABLE[marker]. Find those readers.
REGISTERED_CHUNKS_RESOLVED_2026-08-04.answer: Three read sites, all in the loader region, each reaching a VRAM upload primitive: level_texture_stage 0x8003c8bc @0x8003c920 -> level_texture_upload 0x8003cc58; vram_upload_wait 0x8003c388 @0x8003c3c0 and @0x8003c5ec -> LoadImage 0x800628c0. The registration DEFERS the upload: the loader records where the resource sits, and the frontend uploads it by marker when needed.
REGISTERED_CHUNKS_RESOLVED_2026-08-04.result: Format read off the consumers, then checked against the bytes: 46/46 chunks obey their family's size law EXACTLY, with no free parameter. analysis/phase4_e16_registered_chunks.json

families.A_markers_0x28_0x2F: u32 marker@0, u32 w@+4, u32 h@+8, u32@+12, 16bpp pixels at +16; size == 16 + w*h*2. 3 chunks. The consumer reads 32-bit fields (lw v0,4(s4) / lw v1,8(s4)) and calls LoadImage with addiu a1,s4,16.
families.B_markers_0x30_0x5F: u32 marker@0, u16 w@+4, h@+6, palette_bytes@+8, depth_flag@+10; palette (768 B = 256 x RGB888) at +12, then indexed pixels; size == 12 + palette_bytes + w*h/(1 if depth_flag==1 else 2). 43 chunks: 40 at 8bpp, 3 at 4bpp.

REGISTERED_CHUNKS_RESOLVED_2026-08-04.CORRECTION_to_my_own_correction: Earlier today I corrected 'all 74 unknown chunks are IMAGES' to 'the 46 pointer-registered ones are NOT images -- dimension-shaped u16s are not evidence when the code never reads them as one'. The reasoning was right; the conclusion over-corrected. They ARE images. The loader genuinely never interprets them, but a LATER consumer does, and it reads exactly those dimension fields. What the original claim lacked was a consumer, not a correction -- 'no interpreter HERE' is not 'no interpreter'.
REGISTERED_CHUNKS_RESOLVED_2026-08-04.why_a_static_scan_could_not_settle_it: The consumers index the table (lui at,0x800A; addu at,at,idx; lw v0,DISP(at)), so their displacement is not the table base. A base-displacement sweep over the resident EXE and all 30 .BIN files found 3 stores and 0 reads -- and that clean negative was WRONG. The 0x30..0x57 reader sits at displacement -19032, just outside the [-19224,-19064] base window. A live readwrite watch found all three in one run.
REGISTERED_CHUNKS_RESOLVED_2026-08-04.live_confirmation: analysis/phase4_e16_table_read_watch.json -- boot -> frontend -> Clover Forest on an Interpreter movie, watches armed readwrite so the loader's own registration stores act as the positive control (234 writes, 30 reads, 0 events dropped).
REGISTERED_CHUNKS_RESOLVED_2026-08-04.visual_confirmation: Decoding with the derived layout yields recognisable retail art: marker 0x43 is the memory-card UI text atlas, marker 0x28 the 320x256 title screen. tools/phase4_e16_decode_registered_image.py
REGISTERED_CHUNKS_RESOLVED_2026-08-04.where_they_live: All 46 are in LEVEL00 -- the frontend. The other 28 of the 74 previously-unclassified chunks (markers 0x20 and 0x26) are a different disposition and are unaffected by this.
